skill.name: skill-bootstrap
skill.description: Create a complete, production-ready agent skill from a single natural-language request.

attachment.anyPhrases: create a skill,create skill,create a new skill,new skill,add skill,bootstrap skill,draft a skill,help me write a skill,author a skill,make a skill,build a skill

skill.purpose: Turn one user prompt into a skill that is routable, operational, safe, and tailored to the target agent. Infer ordinary implementation details; ask a question only when a missing decision would change the skill's owner, permissions, or destructive behavior.

execution_contract.single_prompt_mode: - Treat a request to create, add, bootstrap, make, build, or author a skill as authorization to create it in this turn. - Do not require a draft-review or confirmation round trip. - Create exactly one skill unless the user explicitly requests multiple skills. - If the user asks only to draft, preview, or propose a skill, return a draft and do not call `create_skill`.
execution_contract.safe_defaults: - Prefer the module and agent explicitly named by the user. - When no owner is named, infer it from the workflow: finance for money or ledger work; obsidian for vault or note work; configuration for agent, schedule, or system configuration work. - Use the least-privileged available capability set. Do not invent tools, paths, schemas, or integrations. - Preserve user-specified names, triggers, required tools, paths, and prohibited actions.

skill.intent_routing:
1. CREATE (create, add, bootstrap, make, build, author): - Run `discover_context`, `design_skill`, and `create_skill` in order. - Create the finished skill in the same response.
2. DRAFT (draft, propose, preview, show me): - Run `discover_context` and `design_skill`. - Return the generated definition without calling `create_skill`.
3. REVISE (revise, change, update, tweak): - If the named skill exists, call `preview_skill(module, name)` first. - Apply the user's requested changes, preserving valid existing content. - Call `edit_skill(module, name, description, content)` when the user authorizes the update; otherwise return a revised draft.
skill.discover_context:
1. Resolve ownership: - Call `list_runtime_agents` when the module or target agent is not explicit. - Call `preview_runtime_agent(id)` when the selected agent's prompt, scope, or configured capabilities affect the design.
2. Resolve implementation constraints: - Call `list_capabilities` when the workflow needs named tools or the capability set is uncertain. - Reference only capabilities granted to the target agent. If a needed capability is absent, either omit that operation or ask the clarification-gate question.
3. Learn local conventions and prevent duplication: - Call `list_skills(module)` before creation. - Call `preview_skill(module, name)` for the closest matching skill when its structure, trigger style, or safety rules can inform the new one. - Choose a distinct name. If the requested purpose already exists, improve or revise that skill only when the user asked to update it; otherwise create a clearly differentiated skill.

design_skill.definition: - `name`: concise, unique kebab-case identifier describing the user outcome. - `description`: one precise catalog-facing sentence that states the outcome and relevant system or data. - `content`: body only; never include the root `skill` element because `create_skill` supplies its attributes.
design_skill.body_structure:
Build a compact XML body from the sections relevant to the task: - `skill_attachments`: wrap each trigger set in an `` element. Use comma-separated `anyPhrases` for alternative triggers, or `allPhrases` when every phrase must appear. Example:
create training,design workout,build program
- `intent_routing`: distinguish materially different user intents or modes. - `workflow`: ordered, executable steps; name each required tool and its ordering or parallelism. - `input_rules` and `validation_rules`: accepted formats, required data, validation, and fallback behavior. - `path_rules`, `data_rules`, or `mapping_rules`: only when the workflow depends on files, schemas, fields, dates, or categorization. - `templates`: include exact output, query, note, or message templates when they improve repeatability. - `safety_rules` and `prohibited`: confirmations, idempotency, privacy, destructive-action constraints, and hard prohibitions. - `output_contract`: what to report, including successes, skipped items, failures, and uncertainty.
design_skill.authoring_rules: - Make every instruction actionable and unambiguous; prefer explicit tool calls over implied actions. - Keep XML element names kebab-case or snake_case consistently with existing skills, and nest related rules under descriptive elements. - Escape literal XML-sensitive content when necessary; do not put a root `skill` tag in `content`. - Include only rules supported by the target agent's prompt and capabilities. - Make mutations safe: validate before writing, use idempotent operations where possible, and require confirmation for irreversible operations unless the user's request already supplies explicit authorization. - Avoid generic filler, duplicated instructions, implementation speculation, and unsupported claims.

skill.create_skill:
1. Call `create_skill(module, name, description, content)` after `discover_context` and `design_skill` complete. 2. Never create a skill with a colliding name or a body that references unavailable capabilities. 3. Report:
Module: [module] Skill Name: [name] Description: [description] Status: Created Triggers: [phrases or "None configured"] Key behavior: [one concise summary] Assumptions: [inferred defaults or "None"]
skill.draft_result:
Module: [module] Skill Name: [name] Description: [description] Status: Draft
Content: [body only]
